title: Would a Bigger Heart Really Make the Grinch Strong?
summary: Could a small heart make someone grumpy? In Dr. Seuss's How the Grinch Stole Christmas, the Grinch starts with a heart two sizes too small. When he hears joyful singing from Whoville, his heart grows three sizes that day. But would a too-small heart really make someone grumpy, and what would happen if a heart went from too small to really big in an instant? The answer depends on what causes the heart to shrink or grow, experts say, and on whether or not you are a snake. Heart size is generally linked to body size, says heart doctor Michelle Kittleson, though some hearts are naturally bigger or smaller than average. There can be downsides to a too-small heart. In a 2025 study of more than 360,000 people in Australia, those with smaller-than-average hearts had a higher risk of dying within five years, perhaps because smaller hearts may not pump blood as well. Maybe the Grinch's heart was small because he did not exercise enough, Kittleson suggests, and that made him tired and grumpy. But would sudden growth be good for him? The human heart is a four-chambered pump, and there are many ways it can grow, notes molecular biologist Leslie Leinwand. With vigorous exercise, your heart gets bigger in a good way. Pregnancy also makes the heart grow, and if people stop exercising, or give birth, their hearts shrink back to normal size within months. But the Grinch's heart expanded in just moments, more like a snake's. Leinwand studies pythons, whose hearts can grow by up to 25 percent in a day after a large meal, and the bigger the meal, the more the heart grows.
why_it_matters: Understanding how heart size relates to health helps explain why exercise matters for real hearts, not just storybook ones, and why sudden changes in the body can be risky.

background_read: The human heart is a four-chambered pump that moves blood around the body, carrying oxygen and nutrients to every part.
Heart size is usually linked to body size, so bigger bodies tend to have bigger hearts, though some hearts are naturally a bit bigger or smaller than average.
A heart can grow in a healthy way with vigorous exercise, and it can shrink back toward its normal size when exercise stops.
Some animals can change heart size much faster: a python's heart can grow quickly after a large meal, with a bigger meal leading to more growth.
